title.narrative: Supporting MIL development in the Gulf States and Yemen

description.narrative:
The office programming will be focusing on 3 countries: Qatar, Yemen and the UAE. Activities might be led in KSA but are still at the discussion phase (there might be an interest of Riyadh in becoming an MIL city as it is developing to become a leading smart city in the region and entered already in the process of digitalizing its public services + discussion are ongoing with King Saud University Media department to have a long term partnership agreement in which MIL could be a component).
In Qatar, the office will focus on:
- strengthening the collaboration with the Ministry of Education with the long-term objective for MIL to be included in the national curriculum. To do so, the office will build on the national consultation conducted in 2019 and the study on MIL education in K12 schools launched in 2022, to organize in 2024 a multistakeholder national consultation to build a comprehensive program for the upcoming years.
- support the advancement of MIL Cities: contact has been established already in 2023 with cities in Qatar to present the MIL Cities initiative and the process to be followed to become one. End of 2023, a meeting was organized to further explain the process and provide guidance to the interested cities. Doha and Al Rayyan expressed their interest in becoming MIL cities and to launch the process. In 2024, the office will follow-up closely with the cities and provide them with support in the application process. One of the activities will be the multistakeholder national consultation as a dedicated session for MIL Cities is being planned as well a group discussions to allow cities in Qatar to formalize further their partnership and programming with other institutions in the country within their municipality.
- Guidelines and Training program for schools/universities: Building on the results of the national consultation, the office is planning to adapt the new UNESCO MIL Curriculum for Educators and Learner, Media and Information Literate Citizens: Think Critically, Click Wisely to cater to the specific needs of Qatar schools and Universities and to organize a training programme (TOT) for teachers in partnership with Al Jazeera Media Institute. Discussions are ongoing with AJMI to formalize the collaboration, the plan will be proposed to the ministry of Education before the national consultation to be submitted to discussion and approval as an outcome of the consultation.
In the UAE, the office is in discussion with the Dubai Media Council (Media regulatory authority in the Dubai Emirate) to advance MIL in the country. Three areas of collaboration have been identified and still in discussion (a proposal has been sent already that should formalize in a letter of intent in the short term, and MoU):
- Organizations of panel discussions and activities during the Arab Media Forum that will take place in June 2024 in Dubai,
- Celebration of MIL week in Dubai in October 2024 (national consultation and activities related to MIL),
- Supporting Dubai to become and MIL cities.
These first collaborations will aim at sensitizing the country to the importance of MIL and should lead to the building of a more comprehensive plan.
In Yemen, the office will use the potential of MIL to foster peace and understanding in the country, as well as to counter hate speech and disinformation. CI will be mainly focusing on supporting Youth organizations and CSOs as well as Universities and is collaborating closely with ED sector to start working at the school level. The first step to be launched this year will be to conduct a mapping and survey to better understand the state of MIL education in the country and identify the main stakeholders and organizations actively working on the field and using MIL for peace. Through a desk research and meeting with partners, the office has already identified a few initiatives, in particular working on digital skills and MIL for women inclusion. It is to be noted that a few international NGOs are starting since 2023 to work on MIL but not at the national level neither on a large scale but rather supporting small initiatives. On the contrary, the goal of the office is to use the mapping and the survey to build a comprehensive programming at the national level and on a larger scale, a develop a project document that will be presented for donor funding.
The RP budget will be used as seed funding to launch activities that will lead to the development of project proposals/and programs to be submitted to donor funding.
